mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in at least 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in at least 50% of months where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 5% and 3% respectively for three consecutive months signals aggressive monetary tightening amid rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL > 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative or flat 20-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which may reflect precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of such episodes.
